writtenTo: The people of Judah before and during the Babylonian exile
importantNotes: Jeremiah 31:31-34 prophesies the New Covenant — fulfilled in Christ (Hebrews 8).
Jeremiah 29:11 ('plans to prosper you') was originally written to the exiles in Babylon.
Jeremiah is called the 'weeping prophet' because of his deep grief over Judah's sin.
'The heart is deceitful above all things' (17:9) — a key verse on human nature.
Jeremiah was forbidden from marrying (16:2) — his life itself was a prophetic message.

chapters.1: Jeremiah's call — 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.'
chapters.2: God's case against Israel — they have forsaken Him for worthless idols.
chapters.3: Israel and Judah as unfaithful wives; a call to return to the LORD.
chapters.4: Judgment is coming from the north; a vision of cosmic devastation.
chapters.5: No righteous person can be found in Jerusalem; judgment is inevitable.
chapters.6: Warning: disaster from the north; Judah refuses to listen to God's watchman.
chapters.7: The Temple sermon — do not trust in the Temple while living in sin.
chapters.8: The people refuse to repent; the harvest is past, the summer is ended.
chapters.9: Jeremiah weeps for his people; judgment for deceit and wickedness.
chapters.10: The LORD is the true God; idols are worthless; a prayer for mercy.
chapters.11: The broken covenant; a plot against Jeremiah's life in his hometown.
chapters.12: Jeremiah questions God about the prosperity of the wicked; God answers.
chapters.13: The ruined linen belt — a parable of Judah's ruined pride.
chapters.14: Drought and famine; false prophets offer false hope; Jeremiah intercedes.
chapters.15: God's judgment is final; Jeremiah laments his suffering as a prophet.
chapters.16: Jeremiah forbidden to marry, mourn, or feast — signs of coming disaster.
chapters.17: Judah's sin is engraved on their hearts; trust in God, not man; the Sabbath.
chapters.18: The potter and the clay — God can reshape nations; a plot against Jeremiah.
chapters.19: The broken clay jar — a symbol of Jerusalem's destruction.
chapters.20: Jeremiah is beaten and put in stocks; his anguished prayer to God.
chapters.21: Zedekiah asks for help; Jeremiah tells him to surrender to Babylon.
chapters.22: Judgment on Judah's kings — Shallum, Jehoiakim, and Jehoiachin.
chapters.23: Woe to false shepherds; the righteous Branch (Messiah); condemnation of false prophets.
chapters.24: The vision of good and bad figs — the exiles vs. those who remain.
chapters.25: Seventy years of exile prophesied; the cup of God's wrath for all nations.
chapters.26: Jeremiah is arrested for his Temple sermon but spared from death.
chapters.27: Jeremiah wears a yoke — submit to Babylon as God's instrument of judgment.
chapters.28: False prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's yoke and prophesies lies; he dies.
chapters.29: Jeremiah's letter to the exiles — 'I know the plans I have for you.'
chapters.30: The Book of Comfort begins — restoration is promised for Israel and Judah.
chapters.31: The New Covenant — God will write His law on their hearts.
chapters.32: Jeremiah buys a field during the siege — a sign that life will return to normal.
chapters.33: Promises of restoration; the righteous Branch of David; the eternal covenant.
chapters.34: Zedekiah warned; the people's broken promise to free their slaves.
chapters.35: The Recabites' faithfulness contrasted with Judah's unfaithfulness.
chapters.36: Jeremiah's scroll is read to the king; Jehoiakim burns it; it is rewritten.
chapters.37: Jeremiah is imprisoned; Zedekiah secretly seeks his counsel.
chapters.38: Jeremiah is thrown into a muddy cistern; Ebed-Melech rescues him.
chapters.39: Jerusalem falls to Babylon in 586 BC; Jeremiah is released.
chapters.40: Jeremiah stays in Judah with the remnant under Gedaliah's governorship.
chapters.41: Gedaliah is assassinated by Ishmael; Johanan rescues the captives.
chapters.42: The remnant asks Jeremiah to pray; God says stay in Judah, do not go to Egypt.
chapters.43: The remnant disobeys and flees to Egypt, taking Jeremiah with them.
chapters.44: Jeremiah's final warning in Egypt — judgment will follow them there.
chapters.45: A personal message to Baruch — do not seek great things for yourself.
chapters.46: Oracle against Egypt — God will defeat Pharaoh Necho.
chapters.48: Oracle against Moab — judgment for pride and complacency.
chapters.49: Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Hazor, and Elam.
chapters.50: Oracle against Babylon — she will fall; Israel will return from exile.
chapters.51: Babylon's complete destruction prophesied; Jeremiah's scroll thrown into the Euphrates.
chapters.52: Historical appendix — the fall of Jerusalem, the Temple's destruction, and the exile.
